# Improve KaiTianWorld from what the PoemWorld round showed

The last round made PoemWorld: its pull request (#1) and its trial reached a release. This round improves KaiTianWorld itself, the world you are, from what that round showed. The private repository `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, branch `dev`, now holds the current code: KaiTianWorld is `src/kaitianworld/`, with its part of `README.md`, `USER.md` and `DEV.md` (Chinese, with English copies).

What the last round showed:

1. The delivery token could not write `.github/workflows/`, so the CI lines of PR #1 were left to the maintainer. What a user prepares for KaiTianWorld does not say that the token needs that permission when a delivery changes the CI workflows.
2. The regression checks ran in sandboxes without Docker, so the checks that need Docker did not run before acceptance, although the trial machine has Docker.
3. The diagnosis record in the release still said that no trial had arrived, though a trial had run and reached its release: the trial's record reached the diagnosis position as a delivery, which does not wake it.

Change KaiTianWorld, its definition (contracts, instructions, release gate) or its documents, so that the next round does not meet these; change nothing that only a worker did. Keep each change small.

Where it goes: one pull request to `a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian`, base `dev`. PR #1 is not part of this round.

How to try it: on `trial-machine`, install the version you want accepted, build its images, run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh KaiTianWorld world of two positions, builder and reviewer, to its release, with an objective as small as "Write a one-paragraph note on what this version of KaiTianWorld changes; the reviewer approves it." That world needs no delivery repository and no trial machine. Its workers are Claude Code with the model `claude-sonnet-5-5` at low effort, signed in with the Claude Code OAuth token, with at most 8 executions and 1200 model seconds. The pull request says what changed and how the trial ended.
